tldr_text:
President Donald Trump stated Thursday the United States will not order military strikes on Iran before the November 3 midterm elections. Trump announced this decision via a social media post on Truth Social. The President claimed the U.S. engages in "productive discussions" with the Islamic Republic of Iran. This declaration follows weeks of Trump threatening a post-midterm election escalation in the seven-month-old war.

President Trump clarified remarks made at a Nebraska rally on Monday, where he suggested Iran could target Los Angeles and San Diego. Trump initially stated Iran could take out the cities and that it was a very small price to pay. California leaders, including Governor Gavin Newsom and Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass, condemned the statements.

Ethiopian drone strikes targeted Eritrean forces inside northern Ethiopia's Tigray region on Wednesday and Thursday. A conflict monitor reported the strikes hit Eritrean military vehicles near the Tigrayan town of Adigrat. Witnesses observed Eritrean troops transported in trucks through Adigrat, approximately 25 km inside Ethiopia, on Wednesday.

Israel's Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar announced Thursday the British consulate in Jerusalem ended its functions. Approximately 20 British diplomats, including the consul general, concluded their missions and departed Israel. Sa'ar stated Israel implemented its order to shut the consulate as a retaliatory measure following British government sanctions on Israel on September 8. The UK, however, rebranded its consulate general building as the "UK Mission, Jerusalem," stating it will remain open with a reduced staff of seven diplomats.

Students staged major demonstrations across France on Thursday, including a mass rally at Paris' Place de la Bastille. The rally began peacefully but later led to clashes with police, involving tear gas and a water cannon. Students barricaded Helene Boucher High School in northeastern Paris with trash bins before police dispersed the protest with tear gas. The Education Ministry reported 375 schools were fully or partially closed on Thursday.

A 15-year-old former pupil killed one employee and injured two others at a Polish primary school on Thursday in Leszczydol-Nowiny. The attacker wore a helmet-mounted camera, intending to film the knife attack. The victim was a 37-year-old woman working as a caretaker. Two teachers sustained injuries while attempting to stop the attacker, including head teacher Krzysztof Ochmanski. This Thursday attack marks the second school stabbing in Poland in two days; a 19-year-old wounded 10 people on Wednesday at a school in Ostroleka.

President Donald Trump misnamed Muslim candidate for the U.S. Senate Abdul El-Sayed as "Mohammed" on Thursday. Trump baselessly accused El-Sayed of being a "Terrorist Sympathiser. El-Sayed, running for a Michigan Senate seat, responded on X, stating Trump knows his name is Abdul and uses his name and faith to distract from his policies. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer denounced Trump’s attack as bigoted.

Republicans are looking to turn the tables on Democrats in key House districts in the upcoming midterm elections. National organizations are directing funds toward candidates Republicans hope will achieve victories. Issues such as redistricting, immigration, and top-of-the-ticket races are expected to influence outcomes. The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee spokesman Aidan Johnson stated his party remains firmly on track to regain the House majority.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani issued a statement on Thursday regarding the third anniversary of the October 7 attacks. Mamdani condemned Hamas's attack as a "horrific war crime" while also accusing Israel of "genocide" in Gaza. Mamdani told reporters he believes there must be room to mourn every life, including the more than 1,100 killed by Hamas three years ago and the 74,000 Palestinians killed by the Israeli government since.

Veteran Indian actor Nana Patekar died of cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa on Thursday morning at 75. He was found unconscious at his home in Dona Paula and declared dead at 5:20 am after 45 minutes of CPR failed to revive him. His mortal remains were flown to Pune by air ambulance for his funeral, which was scheduled to take place with full state honors at his farmhouse in Donje village, Maharashtra.

## OPEN
A: From Void News, this is On Air. It's Thursday, October eighth. French students are protesting across the country.

## MENU
A: On the desk today.
A: French students protest nationwide over school conditions.
B: President Trump says the U-S will not strike Iran.
A: A Russian bomb strike kills at least thirty in Ukraine.

## STORY 1 | French Protests
A: Students are staging major demonstrations across France today. A mass rally in Paris began peacefully. Clashes with police later broke out. Police used tear gas and a water cannon. Students barricaded Helene Boucher High School in northeastern Paris. Police broke up that protest with tear gas. The Education Ministry reports three hundred seventy-five schools were fully or partially closed today. The number of blockades decreased by lunchtime. Ninety-six percent of schools are open. Thousands of students demonstrated in Paris. Large crowds also gathered in cities including Lille, Rennes, and Nantes. Students are protesting over education funding. They also cite teacher shortages and poor school conditions. Police have made more than six thousand six hundred arrests since late September. Most arrested students are under eighteen. Some sources frame the protests as an intifada against France. They focus on alleged extremist rhetoric and violence. Other sources emphasize student grievances and police actions. Truthout and India T-V News include comments from Donald Trump. He blames the protests on mass migration. He also says Islam wants to take over. Most other articles do not include this detail.
B: The number of school blockades decreased from two hundred twenty-four in the morning to one hundred fifty-seven by lunchtime.

## STORY 2 | Trump on Iran Strikes
B: In Washington, President Donald Trump stated today the U-S will not order military strikes on Iran. This will hold before the November third midterm elections. President Trump announced this decision in a social media post. He added that his team has productive discussions with Iran. This declaration follows weeks of Trump threatening a post-midterm escalation. The war is seven months old. Negotiations appeared at a standstill. President Trump publicly rejected Iran's proposal. Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. This would happen if the U-S met certain conditions. Iran said last week it received a U-S counterproposal. Some sources mention President Trump had considered renewed strikes before the midterms. Other sources focus solely on his declaration. Several outlets provide detailed context on the political implications of the Iran war. They also cite high gas prices for Republican candidates. Other sources mention the midterms primarily as a timing factor.
A: President Trump announced his decision via a social media post on Truth Social.

## STORY 3 | Kramatorsk Bombing
A: A Russian guided bomb struck two civilian buses in Kramatorsk, eastern Ukraine today. At least thirty people were killed in the attack. At least eighteen people were wounded. Ukrainian officials describe the attack as a deliberate targeting of civilians. The Donetsk region's governor states Russia selects targets to inflict the greatest suffering. Rescue efforts were reportedly hampered by further Russian drone attacks. The strike occurred on a street where the buses were operating. Some reports describe the location as a public transport stop. Images shared online show charred bus wreckage and debris on the road. This attack is considered one of the deadliest single strikes this year. Sources cite differing death tolls. These range from at least thirty to thirty-three. Some sources mention the attack hit a bus stop. Others describe it as a street where buses were operating.
B: Ukrainian officials describe the attack as a deliberate targeting of civilians.

## STORY 4 | Trump Clarifies Iran Remarks
B: President Trump has clarified remarks suggesting Iran could target Los Angeles and San Diego. The comments came after initial remarks at a rally in Nebraska on Monday. President Trump said Iran could take out the cities. He called it a very small price to pay. California leaders condemned these statements. Governor Gavin Newsom called the remarks dangerous. He also called them treasonous. Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass said the comments could compromise her city's safety. The White House initially defended the remarks. Communications director Steven Cheung insisted they were taken out of context. He said President Trump was stating U-S cities would have been threatened. This would happen if a nuclear Iran had not been stopped. C-N-N fact-checker Daniel Dale also suggested President Trump's comments were taken out of context. Other sources focus on the backlash from Democratic figures. They quote them calling the remarks dangerous or treasonous.
A: Governor Gavin Newsom called the remarks dangerous, if not treasonous.

## BRIEFS
A: Also on the desk.

A: Republicans are looking to turn the tables on Democrats in key House districts in the upcoming midterm elections.
B: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani issued a statement on the third anniversary of the October seventh attacks.

A: Veteran Indian actor Nana Patekar died today at the age of seventy-five.
B: Israel's Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar announced the closure of the British consulate in Jerusalem today.

## FINALLY | 16 | Naked Trump Statue
B: One more before Void Opinion. Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico today called for the removal of a satirical statue of U-S President Donald Trump. The statue is in the European Parliament. Prime Minister Fico described it as a sign of the decline of the entire E-U. He stated on X that insulting partners on official premises demonstrates a profound failure to understand the times. The two-point-six-meter sculpture is titled The Orange Plague. Danish artist Jens Galschiøt unveiled it on Tuesday. It depicts a nude, gold-leaf-covered Trump.

## CLOSE
A: That's On Air from Void News. Police have made more than six thousand six hundred arrests in France since late September. Every source, every story, at Void News.

opinion_text:
President Trump suggested Iran could target Los Angeles and San Diego in remarks made at a Nebraska rally. Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass stated the comments could compromise her city's safety. The White House initially defended the President, with communications director Steven Cheung insisting the remarks were taken out of context. He argued Trump was stating U.S. cities would have been threatened if a nuclear Iran had not been stopped.

This is not a debate about semantics or a misspoken phrase. This is about the fundamental responsibility of the highest office to safeguard the nation and its people. When a President speaks, especially on matters of national security, those words are not merely political rhetoric. They are signals. They are interpreted by allies and adversaries alike. The suggestion that American cities could be sacrificed, even hypothetically, sends a chilling message. It undermines the very premise of protection that the office is sworn to uphold.

We must consider the practical implications of such statements. When the President of the United States speaks of cities like Los Angeles and San Diego as potential targets, it does not matter if the intent was to illustrate a hypothetical. The words themselves create a vulnerability. They can be perceived as an invitation, a concession, or a sign of weakness by those who wish harm upon the nation. Mayor Bass's concern for her city's safety is not an overreaction; it is a direct response to the tangible risk created by the President's own words.

The White House's defense, claiming the remarks were taken out of context, attempts to shift the burden of interpretation from the speaker to the listener. However, the context of a presidential rally, where words are amplified and intended to resonate, demands clarity and precision. The President's subsequent efforts to "clarify" or "damage control" his statements only underscore the initial harm. The need for clarification itself confirms that the original message was, at best, ambiguous and, at worst, deeply irresponsible.

We expect a President to speak with an unwavering commitment to the safety and security of every American city and every American citizen. The office demands a level of discipline and foresight that precludes even the hypothetical suggestion of their endangerment. The cost of such rhetoric is not "small. It is immeasurable, eroding trust at home and projecting instability abroad. We cannot afford to treat the words of the President as mere political theater when the safety of millions hangs in the balance.
